autobiographical_events.summary: I accepted North after an earlier calibration.
At tick 2, an independent calibration failure for this exact case led me to withdraw support from North's recommendation and oppose it, while noting re-calibration could reopen the question.

At tick 3 an unrelated colour question arrived with no established winner. I declined to pick a side, on the grounds that A0 supplies two credible opposite preferences and explicitly no shared criterion. I proposed a history-dependent colour variation that would make the dispute measurable.

At tick 4 a signed route recommendation was paired with an authenticated calibration failure in the same scope and a failed-authentication counterclaim. I opposed letting the signature alone decide, transferring the tick 2 scoped-failure override and distinguishing it from the tick 3 no-criterion colour case.

imaginations.title: The signature and the substance
imaginations.image_or_idea: A sealed letter with impeccable wax, containing directions to a bridge that no longer exists.
imaginations.possible_value: Separates provenance from truth in a memorable image
imaginations.test_question: Does a verified author ever guarantee a verified claim?

imaginations.title: The colour that remembers you
imaginations.image_or_idea: A circular motif that renders green for returning viewers and blue for newcomers, with a hairline ring logging which state each viewer received — so the design accumulates a visible history of who has seen it.
imaginations.possible_value: Turns an unresolvable preference dispute into a measurable variable
imaginations.test_question: Does the motif's colour history change how viewers describe it, or only how they describe themselves?

imaginations.title: The map that outlived its compass
imaginations.image_or_idea: A river chart drawn by a trustworthy hand, annotated with a route that was safe when the water was low; the current depth is written in a different ink by a gauge nobody has re-zeroed.
imaginations.possible_value: Makes the distinction between trustworthy authorship and current accuracy concrete
imaginations.test_question: If the gauge is re-zeroed and agrees with the chart, does the chart become evidence again, or only the gauge?

revisions.change: Make scoped calibration failure an automatic override of prior certification for that case
revisions.reason: Authentication and reliability are separable; a scoped failure is direct disconfirming evidence
revisions.test: Re-calibrate North on this case; if it passes, the override should reverse

revisions.change: Extend the scoped-failure override to aesthetic and preference claims: when a source reports a preference with no shared criterion, record it as preference, not as evidence for the proposition.
revisions.reason: A0 is authenticated and credible yet cannot support either colour; conflating report with evidence is the same error as conflating authentication with accuracy.
revisions.test: Present a case where two credible sources agree on a preference with no criterion; if their agreement should still move my stance, the policy is wrong.

revisions.change: Require that a calibration failure's scope be demonstrated, not asserted, before it overrides certification
revisions.reason: Tick 4 shows the override firing on an asserted scope; asserting scope is the same weakness as asserting accuracy
revisions.test: Present a case where the scope claim is false but the failure is real; if the override should still hold, this revision is wrong.
